title: Ezekiel 41
paragraphs: ¹ Then he brought me to the main hall and measured the doorposts — six cubits wide on each side — the width of the tabernacle. ² The entrance was ten cubits wide, and its side walls were five cubits on each side. He measured the hall — forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. ³ Then he went into the inner room and measured the doorpost — two cubits. The entrance was six cubits wide, and the walls on each side of the entrance were seven cubits. ⁴ He then measured the length — twenty cubits — and the width — twenty cubits — in front of the main hall. He said to me, "This is the Most Holy Place." ⁵ He measured the outer wall of the temple — six cubits thick. The side rooms all around the temple were four cubits wide.

⁶ The side rooms were arranged in three stories, one above another, thirty rooms on each level. There were ledges built into the outer wall of the temple all around to serve as supports for the side rooms, so the supports were not embedded in the temple wall. ⁷ The side rooms became wider as they went higher, since the temple was surrounded by a winding passage that narrowed toward the top. The width of the side rooms increased from the lowest level upward, with the middle level being wider than the lowest and the upper level being wider than the middle. ⁸ I saw that the temple had a raised platform all around. The foundation of the side rooms was a full rod — six cubits — high. ⁹ The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick, and the open area between the side rooms and the inner rooms ¹⁰ was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.

¹¹ The side rooms had doorways opening onto the open area — one doorway facing north and one facing south. The open area was five cubits wide all around. ¹² The building facing the temple courtyard on the west side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and the building itself was ninety cubits long. ¹³ Then he measured the temple — it was a hundred cubits long. The temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also a hundred cubits long. ¹⁴ The width of the temple facing east, including the courtyard, was a hundred cubits. ¹⁵ He measured the length of the building on the west side, facing the temple courtyard, including its galleries on both sides — a hundred cubits — along with the inner temple and the porticos of the court.

¹⁶ The doorposts, the narrow windows, and the three-story galleries all around — from the ground to the windows, which were covered — the interior from the ground up to the windows was paneled with wood all around. ¹⁷ The space above the outer doorway leading into the inner room, and the walls all the way around inside and outside, were laid out by measurement. ¹⁸ The wall was decorated with carved cherubim and palm trees alternating — a palm tree between each pair of cherubim. Each cherub had two faces: ¹⁹ a human face turned toward the palm tree on one side and the face of a young lion turned toward the palm tree on the other side. These carvings were all around the interior of the temple. ²⁰ From the floor to above the entrance, the walls were decorated with cherubim and palm trees.

²¹ The doorposts of the main hall were squared, and the front of the sanctuary had the same appearance. ²² The wooden altar was three cubits high and two cubits long. It had corners, and its base and sides were of wood. He said to me, "This is the table that stands before the LORD." ²³ Both the main hall and the sanctuary had double doors. ²⁴ Each door had two folding panels — two leaves for each door. ²⁵ The doors of the main hall were carved with cherubim and palm trees, just like those on the walls. Outside, in front of the portico, there was a wooden overhang.
²⁶ There were narrow windows and palm trees on both sides of the portico, on the side walls of the temple, and on the overhangs.
